newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Higher earnings seen for transport cos.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Higher earnings seen for transport cos.

text.p: Trucking companies are expected to report first quarter results surpassing last year's dismal returns, but the outlook isn't as rosy for their rivals on the rails.

Earnings for a number of railroads have been lowered in recent weeks, including those for Illinois Central and Burlington Northern, whose shares fell from the low 80s to the low 70s after announcing March 19 that earnings would be about 20 percent below last year's first quarter results of $1.21.
Argus Research analyst Cornelius Sewell expects first quarter earnings for the rail industry to be off five or 10 percent, mostly due to bad weather.

Railroads expected to beat the industry outlook include Union Pacific, which is expecting first quarter earnings about 50 percent above the year-ago's pro forma $0.32 per share, or about $0.48 a share, said investor relations head Mike Sattler.
Union Pacific is scheduled to report its results Thursday morning in New York.
CSX is comfortable with Wall Street earnings estimates of $0.72 per share for the first quarter, a company spokeswoman said.

The company's rail business, which contributes about 80 percent of total operating income, is expecting another record first quarter on strong traffic in merchandise and coal, she said. CSX is expected to report results April 24.
Earnings expectations for trucking companies are generally brighter than those for railroads.
The trucking industry had a difficult 1996, decimated by high fuel costs, difficult weather and poor pricing conditions mired by excess capacity, analysts said.
"We are looking for very good earnings comparisons for almost all truckload and less-than-truckload carriers, said Alex. Brown analyst Anthony Gallo. "The comparisons are easy."

Gallo sees good numbers for U.S. Xpress, which he thinks will report a fourth quarter profit of $0.16 a share or better, compared to last year's fourth quarter loss, Knight Transportation, which should show a 24 percent increase over its year-ago first quarter, and Covenant Transport, which he thinks will report a $0.12 a share versus $0.04 last year.
Smith Barney analyst Thano Hasiotis said because the industry had such a terrible 1996, year-ago comparisons are not especially meaningful.
"Many companies are going to beat the year-ago estimate," he said, "but there's only one truck-load company that's going to beat what they did two years ago."
Hasiotis said Swift Transportation should beat its 1995 first quarter earnings of $0.16 per share, a notion echoed by Gallo, who believes Swift will report $0.20 for the quarter or better.

Among the better performing regional carriers, Hasiotis picked US Freightways, which last week reported earnings of $0.40 a share, double its year-ago first quarter and up from the 1995 quarter of $0.37.

Of the long-haul carriers, the only company Hasiotis expects to beat its 1995 first quarter earnings is Roadway Express, which reported $0.13 a share in the 1996 quarter and a loss of $0.03 a share in the 1995 quarter.
